claim: Virtually all mitochondrial matrix proteins carry a positively charged, N-terminal presequence.
source: Virtually all mitochondrial matrix proteins and a considerable number of inner membrane proteins carry a positively charged, N-terminal presequence and are imported by the TIM23 complex (presequence translocase) located in the inner mitochondrial membrane.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the abstract without specific experimental data in this manuscript.

claim: A considerable number of inner membrane proteins carry a positively charged, N-terminal presequence.
source: Virtually all mitochondrial matrix proteins and a considerable number of inner membrane proteins carry a positively charged, N-terminal presequence and are imported by the TIM23 complex (presequence translocase) located in the inner mitochondrial membrane.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the abstract.

claim: Presequence-containing proteins are imported by the TIM23 complex located in the inner mitochondrial membrane.
source: Virtually all mitochondrial matrix proteins and a considerable number of inner membrane proteins carry a positively charged, N-terminal presequence and are imported by the TIM23 complex (presequence translocase) located in the inner mitochondrial membrane.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the abstract.

claim: The Tim23 channel is voltage-regulated.
source: The voltage-regulated Tim23 channel constitutes the actual protein-import pore wide enough to allow the passage of polypeptides with a secondary structure.
evidence: This is stated as a known property of Tim23 in the abstract.

claim: The Tim23 channel is wide enough to allow the passage of polypeptides with a secondary structure.
source: The voltage-regulated Tim23 channel constitutes the actual protein-import pore wide enough to allow the passage of polypeptides with a secondary structure.
evidence: This is stated as a known property of Tim23 in the abstract.

claim: Highly conserved, pore-lining amino acids provide selectivity in the Tim23 channel.
source: Structure based mutants show that selectivity is provided by highly conserved, pore-lining amino acids.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study supported by mutagenesis and electrophysiology experiments.

claim: Mutations of selectivity-determining amino acid residues lead to reduced selectivity properties.
source: Mutations of these amino acid residues lead to reduced selectivity properties, reduced protein import capacity and they render the Tim23 channel insensitive to substrates.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by electrophysiological measurements shown in Figure 1.

claim: Mutations of selectivity-determining amino acid residues lead to reduced protein import capacity.
source: Mutations of these amino acid residues lead to reduced selectivity properties, reduced protein import capacity and they render the Tim23 channel insensitive to substrates.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by import assays shown in Figure 4.

claim: Mutations of selectivity-determining amino acid residues render the Tim23 channel insensitive to substrates.
source: Mutations of these amino acid residues lead to reduced selectivity properties, reduced protein import capacity and they render the Tim23 channel insensitive to substrates.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by substrate sensitivity experiments shown in Figure 5.

claim: The cation selectivity of the Tim23 channel is a key feature for substrate recognition.
source: We thus show that the cation selectivity of the Tim23 channel is a key feature for substrate recognition and efficient protein import.
evidence: This is the main conclusion of the study based on the experimental data presented.

claim: The cation selectivity of the Tim23 channel is a key feature for efficient protein import.
source: We thus show that the cation selectivity of the Tim23 channel is a key feature for substrate recognition and efficient protein import.
evidence: This is the main conclusion of the study based on the experimental data presented.

claim: Mitochondria import over 1000 different proteins synthesized on cytosolic ribosomes.
source: Double membrane bounded mitochondria import over 1000 different proteins synthesized on cytosolic ribosomes (Endo and Yamano, 2009; Neupert and Herrmann, 2007; Schmidt et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Approximately 70% of mitochondrial proteins are synthesized with an N-terminal presequence.
source: Approximately, 70% of these mitochondrial proteins are synthesized with an N-terminal presequence (Vögtle et al., 2009), which directs them across the OM.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Vögtle et al., 2009.

claim: The membrane potential (ΔΨ) across the inner membrane exerts an electrophoretic force on positively charged presequences.
source: The membrane potential (ΔΨ) across the energy coupling inner membrane exerts an electrophoretic force on the positively charged presequences, thereby providing energy for the translocation of preproteins.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about the mechanism of protein import.

claim: ΔΨ is necessary and sufficient for membrane insertion of inner membrane proteins.
source: ΔΨ is necessary and sufficient for membrane insertion of IM proteins (van der Laan et al., 2007), whereas full translocation of proteins into the mitochondrial matrix depends on additional energy provided by the ATP consuming presequence translocase-associated import motor PAM (Neupert and Brunner, 2002; Schendzielorz et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Full translocation of proteins into the mitochondrial matrix depends on additional energy provided by the ATP consuming PAM motor.
source: ΔΨ is necessary and sufficient for membrane insertion of IM proteins (van der Laan et al., 2007), whereas full translocation of proteins into the mitochondrial matrix depends on additional energy provided by the ATP consuming presequence translocase-associated import motor PAM (Neupert and Brunner, 2002; Schendzielorz et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: The TIM23 complex consists of the channel forming Tim23 subunit and its homolog Tim17.
source: The TIM23 complex consists of the channel forming Tim23 subunit and its homolog Tim17 (Lohret et al., 1997; Maarse et al., 1994; Meinecke et al., 2006; Ryan et al., 1998; Truscott et al., 2001).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Tim50 is a constitutive subunit of the presequence translocase.
source: Additionally, the receptor protein Tim50 as well as Mgr2 are constitutive subunits of the presequence translocase, whereas Tim21 is specific to the TIM23 complex in the absence of the PAM motor (Chacinska et al., 2005; Ieva et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Mgr2 is a constitutive subunit of the presequence translocase.
source: Additionally, the receptor protein Tim50 as well as Mgr2 are constitutive subunits of the presequence translocase, whereas Tim21 is specific to the TIM23 complex in the absence of the PAM motor (Chacinska et al., 2005; Ieva et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Tim21 is specific to the TIM23 complex in the absence of the PAM motor.
source: Additionally, the receptor protein Tim50 as well as Mgr2 are constitutive subunits of the presequence translocase, whereas Tim21 is specific to the TIM23 complex in the absence of the PAM motor (Chacinska et al., 2005; Ieva et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Tim23 was identified as the central pore-forming component of the TIM23 complex by electrophysiological characterization.
source: Tim23 was identified as the central pore-forming component of the TIM23 complex by electrophysiological characterization of purified Tim23 as well as patch-clamp analyses of inner membrane derived vesicles, depleted of Tim17 (Martinez-Caballero et al., 2007; Truscott et al., 2001).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Tim23 forms a voltage-activated, water-filled pore with a diameter of 1.3–2.4 nm.
source: Tim23 forms a voltage-activated, water-filled pore with a diameter of 1.3–2.4 nm.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge from previous studies.

claim: Tim23 is voltage-regulated by the Tim50 receptor.
source: To maintain the permeability barrier of the inner membrane it is voltage-regulated by the Tim50 receptor and shows sensitivity towards presequence peptides and full-length preproteins (Meinecke et al., 2006; Truscott et al., 2001).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Tim23 shows sensitivity towards presequence peptides and full-length preproteins.
source: To maintain the permeability barrier of the inner membrane it is voltage-regulated by the Tim50 receptor and shows sensitivity towards presequence peptides and full-length preproteins (Meinecke et al., 2006; Truscott et al., 2001).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Tim23 shows a clear preference to conduct cations over anions.
source: Despite its channel dimension, which would allow the simultaneous passage of multiple ions, Tim23 shows a clear preference to conduct cations over anions.
evidence: This is stated as an established property of Tim23.

claim: The selectivity of Tim23 was speculated to be important to recognize and transport positively charged presequences through the channel.
source: Since its discovery this selectivity was speculated to be important to recognize and transport positively charged presequences through the channel.
evidence: This is stated as a historical speculation in the field.

claim: Fluorescent mapping has shown which amino acid residues of the transmembrane helices of Tim23 are likely facing the aqueous channel lumen.
source: Fluorescent mapping has allowed for the first time to show which amino acid residues of the transmembrane helices of Tim23 are likely facing the aqueous channel lumen (Alder et al., 2008; Malhotra et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Tim23G153L exhibits a lethal phenotype.
source: Transformation was successful for all constructs, while 5-FOA selection showed that Tim23G153L exhibited a lethal phenotype as published previously (Demishtein-Zohary et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous literature and confirmed in this study.

claim: Tim23N150A exhibits a significant growth defect on non-fermentable media at 37°C.
source: Four mutants, encoding Tim23N150A, Tim23L155A, Tim23A156L and Tim23Y159A, exhibited a significant growth defect on non-fermentable media at 37°C, with Tim23A156L showing the strongest phenotype (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is supported by growth assay data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Tim23L155A exhibits a significant growth defect on non-fermentable media at 37°C.
source: Four mutants, encoding Tim23N150A, Tim23L155A, Tim23A156L and Tim23Y159A, exhibited a significant growth defect on non-fermentable media at 37°C, with Tim23A156L showing the strongest phenotype (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is supported by growth assay data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Tim23A156L exhibits a significant growth defect on non-fermentable media at 37°C.
source: Four mutants, encoding Tim23N150A, Tim23L155A, Tim23A156L and Tim23Y159A, exhibited a significant growth defect on non-fermentable media at 37°C, with Tim23A156L showing the strongest phenotype (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is supported by growth assay data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Tim23Y159A exhibits a significant growth defect on non-fermentable media at 37°C.
source: Four mutants, encoding Tim23N150A, Tim23L155A, Tim23A156L and Tim23Y159A, exhibited a significant growth defect on non-fermentable media at 37°C, with Tim23A156L showing the strongest phenotype (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is supported by growth assay data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Tim23A156L shows the strongest growth defect phenotype among the mutants tested.
source: Four mutants, encoding Tim23N150A, Tim23L155A, Tim23A156L and Tim23Y159A, exhibited a significant growth defect on non-fermentable media at 37°C, with Tim23A156L showing the strongest phenotype (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is supported by growth assay data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Tim23N150A exhibits a significantly reduced reversal potential.
source: Interestingly, in a wide screen for basic electrophysiological parameters we found that a number of mutants (Tim23N150A, Tim23A156L, Tim23Y159A) that showed growth defects exhibited a significantly reduced reversal potential (Figures 1D and 3D and Figure 1—figure supplement 1B), which translates to a severe reduction of the channels cation preference (Figure 1E), while other parameters remained unaffected (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B–D).
evidence: This is supported by electrophysiological data shown in Figures 1D, 3D, and Figure 1—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Tim23A156L exhibits a significantly reduced reversal potential.
source: Interestingly, in a wide screen for basic electrophysiological parameters we found that a number of mutants (Tim23N150A, Tim23A156L, Tim23Y159A) that showed growth defects exhibited a significantly reduced reversal potential (Figures 1D and 3D and Figure 1—figure supplement 1B), which translates to a severe reduction of the channels cation preference (Figure 1E), while other parameters remained unaffected (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B–D).
evidence: This is supported by electrophysiological data shown in Figures 1D, 3D, and Figure 1—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Tim23Y159A exhibits a significantly reduced reversal potential.
source: Interestingly, in a wide screen for basic electrophysiological parameters we found that a number of mutants (Tim23N150A, Tim23A156L, Tim23Y159A) that showed growth defects exhibited a significantly reduced reversal potential (Figures 1D and 3D and Figure 1—figure supplement 1B), which translates to a severe reduction of the channels cation preference (Figure 1E), while other parameters remained unaffected (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B–D).
evidence: This is supported by electrophysiological data shown in Figures 1D, 3D, and Figure 1—figure supplement 1B.

claim: The selectivity of Tim23N150A dropped down to 33% of wild type level.
source: The strongest reduction was observed for Tim23N150A, where the selectivity dropped down to 33% of wild type level.
evidence: This is supported by selectivity measurements shown in Figure 1E.

claim: Tim23G153A shows a reduction in cation preference to between 50–70% of wild type level.
source: A slightly weaker reduction in cation preference (between 50–70% of wild type level) was observed for Tim23G153A, Tim23A156G, Tim23A156L, Tim23Y159A and Tim23N160A.
evidence: This is supported by selectivity measurements shown in Figure 1E.

claim: Tim23A156G shows a reduction in cation preference to between 50–70% of wild type level.
source: A slightly weaker reduction in cation preference (between 50–70% of wild type level) was observed for Tim23G153A, Tim23A156G, Tim23A156L, Tim23Y159A and Tim23N160A.
evidence: This is supported by selectivity measurements shown in Figure 1E.

claim: Tim23A156L shows a reduction in cation preference to between 50–70% of wild type level.
source: A slightly weaker reduction in cation preference (between 50–70% of wild type level) was observed for Tim23G153A, Tim23A156G, Tim23A156L, Tim23Y159A and Tim23N160A.
evidence: This is supported by selectivity measurements shown in Figure 1E.

claim: Tim23Y159A shows a reduction in cation preference to between 50–70% of wild type level.
source: A slightly weaker reduction in cation preference (between 50–70% of wild type level) was observed for Tim23G153A, Tim23A156G, Tim23A156L, Tim23Y159A and Tim23N160A.
evidence: This is supported by selectivity measurements shown in Figure 1E.

claim: Tim23N160A shows a reduction in cation preference to between 50–70% of wild type level.
source: A slightly weaker reduction in cation preference (between 50–70% of wild type level) was observed for Tim23G153A, Tim23A156G, Tim23A156L, Tim23Y159A and Tim23N160A.
evidence: This is supported by selectivity measurements shown in Figure 1E.

claim: All residues with decreased selectivity are highly conserved between Tim23 in different species.
source: All residues with decreased selectivity are highly conserved between Tim23 in different species (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is supported by sequence alignment data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: Reduced levels of Tim23 were found for the mutants Tim23L155A, Tim23A156L, Tim23Y159A and Tim23N160A.
source: Reduced levels of Tim23 were found for the mutants Tim23L155A, Tim23A156L, Tim23Y159A and Tim23N160A (Figure 2A, lanes 5, 7, 8 and 9).
evidence: This is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: TIM23 and PAM subunits could be efficiently co-purified in co-immunoprecipitation experiments.
source: Interestingly, TIM23 and PAM subunits could be efficiently co-purified.
evidence: This is supported by co-immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: The TIM23 complex remained intact in Tim23N150A and Tim23Y159A mutants as assessed by size exclusion chromatography.
source: In agreement with the results of the immunoisolation analyses, the TIM23 complex apparently remained intact and associated with the import motor (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by size exclusion chromatography data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: Tim23N150A was the only mutation that led to impaired growth, decreased ion-selectivity and exhibited normal protein levels and complex assembly.
source: Hence, after carefully testing the suitability of Tim23 mutants for subsequent analysis, Tim23N150A was the only mutation that led to impaired growth, decreased ion-selectivity and exhibited normal protein levels and complex assembly and was therefore further analyzed in in organello assays.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the combined data from growth assays, electrophysiology, and protein level measurements.

claim: All protein levels in mitochondria from Tim23N150A expressing cells were unchanged compared to wild type.
source: Mitochondrial steady state levels of selected proteins were analyzed, that is, TIM23 complex components, PAM complex subunits and mitochondrial marker proteins (Figure 2C). Here, all protein levels in mitochondria from Tim23N150A expressing cells were unchanged compared to wild type.
evidence: This is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: The inner membrane potential was not affected in mitochondria containing Tim23N150A.
source: To assess that the inner membrane potential was not affected in mitochondria containing Tim23N150A, we tested the ΔΨ in organello, using the membrane-permeable fluorophore DiSC3(5) (Figure 2D). The measurements showed that ΔΨ was not significantly altered in Tim23N150A-expressing cells compared to the wild type control (Figure 2D and E).
evidence: This is supported by fluorescence measurements shown in Figure 2D and E.

claim: The IMS domain of Tim50 exhibited the same voltage-regulation on wild type and Tim23N150A.
source: In agreement with this unchanged membrane potential, in single-channel measurements the IMS domain of Tim50 exhibited the same voltage-regulation on wild type and Tim23N150A that we reported before (Figure 3E and F) (Meinecke et al., 2006).
evidence: This is supported by electrophysiological data shown in Figure 3E and F.

claim: Wild type Tim23 and Tim23N150A channels exhibited complex voltage-dependent gating patterns.
source: Wild type as well as Tim23N150A channels exhibited complex voltage-dependent gating patterns (Figure 3A and B).
evidence: This is supported by electrophysiological recordings shown in Figure 3A and B.

claim: Both wild type Tim23 and Tim23N150A pores gated with the same main-conductance state of ~460 pS at 250 mM KCl.
source: Both pores gated with the same main-conductance state of ~460 pS (at 250 mM KCl) and showed similar sub-conductance states of ~170 pS and ~60 pS (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is supported by conductance analysis shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Wild type Tim23 and Tim23N150A showed similar sub-conductance states of ~170 pS and ~60 pS.
source: Both pores gated with the same main-conductance state of ~460 pS (at 250 mM KCl) and showed similar sub-conductance states of ~170 pS and ~60 pS (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is supported by conductance analysis shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Tim23N150A displayed a reduced reversal potential compared to wild type.
source: Again Tim23N150A displayed a reduced reversal potential, while the wild type and mutant Tim23 showed the same voltage-dependent open probability (Figure 3E and F) and were efficiently voltage-regulated by Tim50IMS as published before (Figure 3E and F) (Meinecke et al., 2006).
evidence: This is supported by electrophysiological data shown in Figure 3E and F.

claim: Wild type and mutant Tim23 showed the same voltage-dependent open probability.
source: Again Tim23N150A displayed a reduced reversal potential, while the wild type and mutant Tim23 showed the same voltage-dependent open probability (Figure 3E and F) and were efficiently voltage-regulated by Tim50IMS as published before (Figure 3E and F) (Meinecke et al., 2006).
evidence: This is supported by electrophysiological data shown in Figure 3E and F.

claim: Tim23N150A is found in wild type levels in mitochondria.
source: In summary, Tim23N150A is found in wild type levels in mitochondria, integrates properly into the TIM23 complex, and has no effect on the integrity of the inner membrane.
evidence: This is a summary statement based on data shown in Figure 2.

claim: Tim23N150A integrates properly into the TIM23 complex.
source: In summary, Tim23N150A is found in wild type levels in mitochondria, integrates properly into the TIM23 complex, and has no effect on the integrity of the inner membrane.
evidence: This is a summary statement based on data shown in Figure 2.

claim: Tim23N150A has no effect on the integrity of the inner membrane.
source: In summary, Tim23N150A is found in wild type levels in mitochondria, integrates properly into the TIM23 complex, and has no effect on the integrity of the inner membrane.
evidence: This is a summary statement based on membrane potential measurements shown in Figure 2D and E.

claim: Tim23N150A displays wild type-like channel characteristics except for a significantly reduced cation preference.
source: In addition, it displays wild type-like channel characteristics except for a significantly reduced cation preference.
evidence: This is a summary statement based on electrophysiological data shown in Figure 3.

claim: Import efficiency of F1β into Tim23N150A mitochondria is significantly reduced.
source: Even at permissive temperature, quantified import efficiency in the linear phase revealed significant reductions for both types of imported substrates (Figure 4E), showing that Tim23N150A is clearly affected in protein import.
evidence: This is supported by import assay data shown in Figure 4A and 4E.

claim: Import efficiency of Cox4 into Tim23N150A mitochondria is significantly reduced.
source: Even at permissive temperature, quantified import efficiency in the linear phase revealed significant reductions for both types of imported substrates (Figure 4E), showing that Tim23N150A is clearly affected in protein import.
evidence: This is supported by import assay data shown in Figure 4B and 4E.

claim: Import efficiency of b2(167)Δ-DHFR into Tim23N150A mitochondria is significantly reduced.
source: Even at permissive temperature, quantified import efficiency in the linear phase revealed significant reductions for both types of imported substrates (Figure 4E), showing that Tim23N150A is clearly affected in protein import.
evidence: This is supported by import assay data shown in Figure 4C and 4E.

claim: Import efficiency of b2(220)-DHFR into Tim23N150A mitochondria is significantly reduced.
source: Even at permissive temperature, quantified import efficiency in the linear phase revealed significant reductions for both types of imported substrates (Figure 4E), showing that Tim23N150A is clearly affected in protein import.
evidence: This is supported by import assay data shown in Figure 4D and 4E.

claim: Import experiments conducted at 37°C show an even more pronounced reduction in import efficiency for Tim23N150A.
source: Import experiments conducted at 37°C show the same trend with an even more pronounced reduction (Figure 4—figure supplement 1), while import experiments using the ADP/ATP carrier (AAC) and Cox12 revealed that other import pathways into mitochondria (TIM22 and MIA) were not impaired by the mutation (Figure 4F and G).
evidence: This is supported by import assay data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: Other import pathways into mitochondria (TIM22 and MIA) were not impaired by the Tim23N150A mutation.
source: Import experiments conducted at 37°C show the same trend with an even more pronounced reduction (Figure 4—figure supplement 1), while import experiments using the ADP/ATP carrier (AAC) and Cox12 revealed that other import pathways into mitochondria (TIM22 and MIA) were not impaired by the mutation (Figure 4F and G).
evidence: This is supported by import assay data shown in Figure 4F and G.

claim: Wild type Tim23 showed a distinct activity increase characterized by fast gating after addition of Cox4 presequence peptide.
source: Wild type Tim23 showed a distinct activity increase, characterized by fast gating (flickering), after addition of Cox4 (Figure 5A,B and C).
evidence: This is supported by electrophysiological recordings shown in Figure 5A, B, and C.

claim: Tim23N150A responded with an increased gating frequency to Cox4 addition, but the effect was drastically reduced compared to wild type Tim23.
source: While Tim23N150A also responded with an increased gating frequency to Cox4 addition, the effect was drastically reduced in comparison to wild type Tim23.
evidence: This is supported by electrophysiological recordings shown in Figure 5.

claim: Wild type Tim23 channels could be activated to a relative increase in gating frequency of factor 50.
source: Where wild type Tim23 channels could be activated to a relative increase in gating frequency of factor 50 (Figure 5D, black curve), the gating frequency of Tim23N150A only changed by a factor 6 (Figure 5D, red curve), resulting in an 88% reduction of voltage-activated gating from wild type to mutant Tim23.
evidence: This is supported by quantification of gating frequency shown in Figure 5D.

claim: The gating frequency of Tim23N150A only changed by a factor 6 in response to Cox4 presequence peptide.
source: Where wild type Tim23 channels could be activated to a relative increase in gating frequency of factor 50 (Figure 5D, black curve), the gating frequency of Tim23N150A only changed by a factor 6 (Figure 5D, red curve), resulting in an 88% reduction of voltage-activated gating from wild type to mutant Tim23.
evidence: This is supported by quantification of gating frequency shown in Figure 5D.

claim: There is an 88% reduction of voltage-activated gating from wild type to mutant Tim23N150A.
source: Where wild type Tim23 channels could be activated to a relative increase in gating frequency of factor 50 (Figure 5D, black curve), the gating frequency of Tim23N150A only changed by a factor 6 (Figure 5D, red curve), resulting in an 88% reduction of voltage-activated gating from wild type to mutant Tim23.
evidence: This is calculated from the data shown in Figure 5D.

claim: Both wild type Tim23 and Tim23N150A have near identical average gating frequencies in unstimulated conditions.
source: To further prove that the relative reduction in gating frequency did not originate from e.g. a higher baseline of gating frequency of Tim23N150A compared to wild type Tim23, we analyzed absolute gating frequencies in the absence of substrate peptides (Figure 5E). Both proteins have near identical average gating frequencies in unstimulated conditions, excluding pre-activation effects.
evidence: This is supported by gating frequency analysis shown in Figure 5E.

claim: A decreased selectivity of Tim23 leads to reduced substrate sensitivity.
source: In summary, our data show that a decreased selectivity of Tim23 leads to reduced substrate sensitivity, which explains the impaired protein import capacity of mitochondria expressing a Tim23 selectivity mutant.
evidence: This is the main conclusion based on the combined data from electrophysiology and import assays.

claim: Reduced substrate sensitivity explains the impaired protein import capacity of mitochondria expressing a Tim23 selectivity mutant.
source: In summary, our data show that a decreased selectivity of Tim23 leads to reduced substrate sensitivity, which explains the impaired protein import capacity of mitochondria expressing a Tim23 selectivity mutant.
evidence: This is the main conclusion based on the combined data from electrophysiology and import assays.

claim: Tim23 was identified as the import channel for presequence carrying substrates more than 15 years ago.
source: Tim23, the eponymous core subunit of the TIM23 complex, was identified as the import channel for presequence carrying substrates more than 15 years ago (Lohret et al., 1997; Truscott et al., 2001).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: A number of different residues are involved in discriminating between ions in Tim23.
source: Interestingly, we found that a number of different residues are involved in discriminating between ions.
evidence: This is a finding of the study based on mutagenesis and electrophysiology experiments.

claim: All amino acids detected to be important for channel selectivity are strictly conserved in evolution.
source: All amino acids detected to be important for channel selectivity are strictly conserved in evolution, suggesting an essential role for the selectivity in protein transport across the inner membrane.
evidence: This is based on sequence alignment data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: The strict conservation of selectivity-determining amino acids suggests an essential role for the selectivity in protein transport across the inner membrane.
source: All amino acids detected to be important for channel selectivity are strictly conserved in evolution, suggesting an essential role for the selectivity in protein transport across the inner membrane.
evidence: This is an inference based on the conservation data.

claim: Selectivity-determining residues were successfully cross-linked to preproteins in transit in recent studies.
source: In recent studies these residues were successfully cross-linked to preproteins in transit, showing their accessibility and exposure to the channel lumen (Alder et al., 2008; Malhotra et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Selectivity is not necessarily provided by a confined restriction zone within the channel but rather by specific channel surface characteristics throughout the length of the pore.
source: Our results imply that selectivity is not necessarily provided by a confined restriction zone within the channel but rather by specific channel surface characteristics throughout the length of the pore, which facilitate the passage of certain ions over others.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the results based on the finding that multiple residues contribute to selectivity.

claim: A similar mechanism for selectivity was proposed for other large pores.
source: Such a mechanism was proposed for other large pores to explain their selective properties (Im and Roux, 2002; Kutzner et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Tim23G153A shows a mediocre reduction in selectivity while growth is relatively unaffected.
source: As an outlier Tim23G153A shows a mediocre reduction in selectivity while growth is relatively unaffected and we therefore hypothesize that a certain impairment of the selective properties can be compensated.
evidence: This is based on data shown in Figures 1C and 1E.

claim: A certain impairment of the selective properties can be compensated.
source: As an outlier Tim23G153A shows a mediocre reduction in selectivity while growth is relatively unaffected and we therefore hypothesize that a certain impairment of the selective properties can be compensated.
evidence: This is a hypothesis based on the observation that Tim23G153A has reduced selectivity but normal growth.

claim: The position of the amino acid substitution N150A is found close to the beginning of transmembrane helix 2 and is therefore located at the matrix side of the channel.
source: The position of the amino acid substitution N150A is found close to the beginning of transmembrane helix 2 and is therefore located at the matrix side of the channel.
evidence: This is based on structural knowledge of Tim23.

claim: The substrate has to reach deep into the channel to be affected by a mutation at the matrix side.
source: This suggests that the decreased substrate sensitivity characterized by an inactive, slowly gating channel in the presence of prepeptides cannot be explained by binding and activation of the substrate to the IMS side of the channel. Instead the substrate has to reach deep into the channel to be affected by a mutation at the matrix side.
evidence: This is an inference based on the location of the N150A mutation and its effect on substrate sensitivity.

claim: The active, fast-gating Tim23 is likely a transport competent state of the channel, triggered by peptides in transit within the channel that are discriminated by the channels selective properties.
source: Similar to what was described for Tom40 (Mahendran et al., 2012), the active, fast-gating Tim23 is therefore likely a transport competent state of the channel, triggered by peptides in transit within the channel that are discriminated by the channels selective properties.
evidence: This is an inference based on the data and comparison to Tom40.

claim: A decreased selectivity of Tim23 leads to an inability to be activated and therefore directly to decreased import rates.
source: A decreased selectivity of Tim23 leads to an inability to be activated and therefore directly to decreased import rates.
evidence: This is the main mechanistic conclusion of the study based on the combined data.

claim: Water-filled pores were identified at the heart of most organellar translocation complexes.
source: While water-filled pores were identified at the heart of most organellar translocation complexes (du Plessis et al., 2011; Harsman et al., 2010; Meinecke et al., 2016; Neupert and Herrmann, 2007; Schmidt et al., 2010; Sjuts et al., 2017), only basic channel characteristics were described in most cases.
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Tim23, Tim22, Tom40 and Sam50 all display comparable channel diameters and a preference for cations.
source: Although structurally diverse, Tim23, Tim22, Tom40 and Sam50 all display comparable channel diameters and a preference for cations.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about these channels.
